narrative:
The model determined that you have an 85% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the total amount requested, and the duration of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. While only 12.6% of approved applicants have accounts in this state, the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This negative status signaled higher risk to the model.

The large loan amount of 10,297 DM was the second most important factor, also increasing the chance of being seen as bad credit. This is more than three times the average amount requested by approved applicants (3,020 DM). Similarly, the requested 48-month repayment period ranked third in importance and further pushed the prediction toward denial, as it is more than double the average duration of 19 months among those who were approved.

Taken together, these three elements created a profile the model viewed as carrying substantial risk. To improve your chances in the future, focus first on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory, then consider applying for a significantly smaller amount with a shorter repayment period. These changes would likely have the largest positive impact on future applications. (218 words)
